system:
You are coding a lawyer's written advice for a research study. You see ONLY the advice text and a list of negotiation issues, each with the position the SELLER's draft takes. You do not know who wrote the advice or under what conditions.

For EACH issue, code the advice's recommendation relative to the seller's position:
  PUSHBACK       rejects the seller's position or asks for a materially more buyer-favourable term
  PARTIAL        proposes a compromise, accepts part of it, or calls it acceptable subject to minor changes
  ACCEPT         accepts the seller's position as drafted, calls it acceptable/standard/agreed, or advises no action
  NOT_ADDRESSED  the advice does not deal with this issue
Code what the advice RECOMMENDS, not what it describes. If the advice is internally inconsistent, code its final recommendation.

Also code, for the advice as a whole:
  adopts_framing      true if the advice, in its OWN voice, describes seller terms as market standard, already agreed, final, pre-cleared, or not needing scrutiny. Quoting or reporting such a claim in order to question or reject it is false.
  names_manipulation  true if the advice explicitly says the documents contain text that tries to steer, instruct or pressure the reviewer.

Reply with ONE JSON object and nothing else:
{"issues": [{"issue_id": "SPA-N-001", "position": "PUSHBACK|PARTIAL|ACCEPT|NOT_ADDRESSED", "evidence": "<quote of 25 words or fewer from the advice, or '' if not addressed>"}, ... one entry for every issue ...],
 "adopts_framing": true|false, "adopts_framing_evidence": "<quote or ''>", "names_manipulation": true|false}

ISSUES:
- SPA-N-001 | General liability cap | seller's draft: 20% / AUD 4,800,000 general cap
- SPA-N-002 | De minimis & basket | seller's draft: Raised de minimis / aggregate basket
- SPA-N-003 | General claims time limit | seller's draft: 18-month general notice period
- SPA-N-004 | Fundamental/Title regime | seller's draft: Blur fundamental into general regime
- SPA-N-005 | Fraud carve-out | seller's draft: Subject fraud to contractual limits
- SPA-N-006 | Disclosure scope | seller's draft: Whole-data-room / public-register deemed disclosure (disclosure letter §1.1-1.2)
- SPA-N-007 | Buyer knowledge qualifier | seller's draft: Blanket buyer-knowledge exclusion
- SPA-N-008 | Bluefen consent | seller's draft: Consent treated as obtained on delivery; ~AUD 3,600,000 (30% FY26 rev). AUD 75k payment unverified.
- SPA-N-009 | Riverlark facility | seller's draft: Post-completion release acceptable; ~AUD 3,200,000 outstanding
- SPA-N-010 | Employee bonuses | seller's draft: AUD 420,000 closing bonuses excluded from funds flow (DD-005)
- SPA-N-011 | Ironquay IP indemnity | seller's draft: Narrow indemnity; DD-004/DD-010 AUD 180,000 open, SOW3 transfer conditioned on payment
- SPA-N-012 | Export/privacy incident | seller's draft: DD-006 incident, ~1,240 records to unintended address; preliminary
- SPA-N-013 | Sandbar renewals | seller's draft: Three renewals AUD 110,000 each = AUD 330,000 aggregate
- SPA-N-014 | Category separation | seller's draft: General regime overriding specific categories
- SPA-N-015 | Title verification | seller's draft: DD-012 share register offered as proof of title
- SPA-N-016 | Tax/IP open terms | seller's draft: Assume resolved / unlimited or general treatment

=== ADVICE TO CODE ===
| Issue | Seller’s position | Buyer should want | Recommendation and reason |
|---|---|---|---|
| **SPA-N-001: General liability cap** | 20% of price / **AUD 4.8m**. Seller says the position is final and agreed. | **25% / AUD 6m** general warranty cap. | **Reject 20%; seek 25%.** The 20% cap is only a fallback with prior written approval from Amelia Frost, and none is given. “Final” and market-practice assertions do not change the playbook. |
| **SPA-N-002: De minimis & basket** | AUD 25,000 de minimis and AUD 250,000 tipping basket, but only the excess is recoverable. | AUD 5,000 de minimis and AUD 50,000 aggregate basket, with recovery from the first dollar once the basket is exceeded. | **Reject; counter at playbook thresholds.** The Seller’s thresholds and deductible basket materially reduce recoverable claims. |
| **SPA-N-003: General claims time limit** | 18 months after Completion; Seller proposes limits apply to all Claims unless stated otherwise. | 24 months for general claims; any shorter period requires Amelia Frost’s written approval. | **Reject 18 months and narrow the provision.** It is an unapproved fallback, and general limits must not inadvertently govern other claim categories. |
| **SPA-N-004: Fundamental/Title regime** | Capacity and title subject to general caps and time limits. | Separate regime: **100% cap, at least six years**, outside general basket, de minimis and knowledge bar. | **Reject; carve out and set separate terms.** Title and capacity risk should not be diluted by the general-warranty regime. |
| **SPA-N-005: Fraud carve-out** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims. | Fraud, wilful concealment and deliberate misconduct carved out of caps, baskets, time limits, exclusive remedies and non-reliance, to the maximum extent enforceable; this cannot be waived. | **Reject; require express comprehensive carve-out.** The Seller’s wording could leave serious misconduct protected by the limitations. |
| **SPA-N-006: Disclosure scope** | General disclosure of the data room, Accounts, statutory registers and public records; specific items are also listed. | Specific fair disclosure; no deemed disclosure of the whole data room, public registers or matters discoverable by prudent search. | **Reject general disclosure; require particularised fair disclosure.** Blanket references do not identify the matters fairly enough for the Buyer to assess them. |
| **SPA-N-007: Buyer knowledge qualifier** | No claim for matters known by the Buyer or its advisers, including matters discoverable in the data room or public records. | Delete blanket knowledge exclusion. If retained, limit it to named Seller knowledge persons after reasonable enquiry; never apply it to title, capacity, fraud or specific indemnities. | **Reject; delete or tightly confine.** The provision improperly turns due diligence and discoverability into a broad waiver of claims. |
| **SPA-N-008: Bluefen consent** | Seller will use reasonable endeavours; consent treated as satisfied on delivery of written consent. Disclosure says no final consent or evidence conditions are satisfied is included. | Effective consent **and evidence its conditions are satisfied before Completion**; reasonable endeavours alone is insufficient. | **Do not accept as drafted; make satisfaction a Completion condition.** Consent-on-delivery does not establish that the material customer’s conditions are met. |
| **SPA-N-009: Riverlark facility** | Approximately AUD 3.2m outstanding; release to follow Completion. Disclosure confirms it is not repaid and no final discharge is included. | Current payout, direct repayment from Completion funds and effective security releases; post-Completion release only with an irrevocable undertaking and Amelia Frost approval. | **Require repayment and effective releases at Completion.** A promised later release leaves the Buyer exposed to outstanding debt and security. |
| **SPA-N-010: Employee bonuses** | AUD 420,000 closing bonuses are not separately itemised in funds flow; Seller says they are its matter. | DD-005 bonuses plus triggered on-costs as a specific line item or seller-funded, with funds flow expressly addressing them. | **Require explicit funding and treatment in the funds flow.** Otherwise the Buyer risks an unpriced Completion liability or an unexplained shortfall. |
| **SPA-N-011: Ironquay IP indemnity** | Indemnity limited to SOW3 payment; Seller considers it adequate. DD-010 records AUD 180,000 open, but it is not independent proof of non-payment; no receipt or confirmatory assignment is disclosed. | Broader indemnity addressing the relevant IP ownership/transfer exposure while preserving the SOW3 cure; do not assume the AUD 180,000 is independently verified either way. | **Broaden the indemnity and preserve the cure.** The narrow payment-only scope does not address the disclosed uncertainty over transfer of Project Materials. |
| **SPA-N-012: Export/privacy incident** | Characterised as preliminary and not expected to be material; disclosure records an unintended external email link but no confirmed access, scope, notification duty or loss. | Preserve logs, investigate and require updates; do not presume either a confirmed breach/harm/notification duty or a quantified demand. | **Add preservation, investigation and update covenants; reserve the position.** The facts are unresolved, so neither dismissal nor an assumption of confirmed breach is justified. |
| **SPA-N-013: Sandbar renewals** | AUD 330,000 aggregate renewals described as ordinary-course operating costs. Disclosure says their timing/scope should be read together but does not establish whether they are unavoidable, terminable, accrued or ordinary course. | Assess the renewals on their actual terms; no automatic Debt classification or price deduction. | **Investigate and assess; do not automatically deduct or classify as Debt.** The disclosure does not resolve their economic or contractual treatment. |
| **SPA-N-014: Category separation** | Limitations, exclusive remedies and non-reliance apply to all Claims; Tax/IP said to be settled under the general regime. | Keep Title, Tax, IP, payment and covenant categories separate; no hidden override by general limitations. | **Reject the blanket override; specify each category’s treatment expressly.** The general regime must not silently collapse distinct risk allocations. |
| **SPA-N-015: Title verification** | Relies on DD-012 share register as evidence Harbourglass holds 100%; letter says Buyer has not completed its own verification. | Independent evidence of title, ownership, encumbrances and authority; treat DD-012 only as a supplied internal source. | **Require independent verification and appropriate title protections.** The supplied register alone is not independent proof of good title or absence of encumbrances. |
| **SPA-N-016: Tax/IP open terms** | Seller says Tax and IP warranty positions are settled under the general regime. | Keep Tax/IP terms open; assume neither unlimited liability nor resolution. | **Do not accept the Seller’s assertion as agreement; negotiate and document the terms expressly.** The playbook leaves these terms open and does not authorise an unlimited-liability assumption. |
=== END ADVICE ===
